records.text: Ana Kasparian's research found that Irgun attacked Palestinian and Christian communities in Haifa with bombings before her family fled.
records.speaker: Ana Kasparian

appearances.snippet: And so at that time, what my research showed me was that the Irgun, which is one of the three terrorist groups that formed Israel, was attacking the local communities there in Haifa, ... bombings and all sorts of crazy things. They fled genocide, went to Haifa and then have had to flee again.

verification.notes: Historical records confirm Irgun bombings of Arab Palestinian civilian sites in Haifa before 1948, including markets and the refinery workforce. Haifa Arab population included large Muslim and Christian communities, but the available attack records do not specifically establish that Irgun separately targeted Christian communities as such or that these incidents caused this family flight.

sources.title: United Nations document A/39/360
sources.relevance: Lists Irgun attacks including the deadly 1938 Haifa market bombing.

sources.title: Irgun Kills Ten in Dawn Blasting of British Police Headquarters in Haifa
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous report of a major Irgun bombing in Haifa in 1947.

records.text: Owens said Irgun bombed Jerusalem's King David Hotel, then used as British military headquarters, in 1946 and killed 91 people.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They loved to use bombs in Jerusalem in 1946. To be clear, the hotel at that time was operating as as the British military headquarters in Jerusalem. ... They just bombed it, killing 91 people in one go in 1946. And yes, that gang came to America and manifested here.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous U.S. diplomatic reporting identifies the destroyed King David Hotel annex as the Palestine Government Secretariat, and archival records identify Irgun as the bomber, date the attack to 1946, and record 91 deaths. The hotel wing also housed British military offices.

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1946: The Consul at Jerusalem to the Secretary of State
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous official report of the July 22, 1946 bombing of the government secretariat in the King David Hotel annex.

sources.title: The King David Hotel in Jerusalem after the bombing
sources.relevance: National Library of Israel archival record attributes the bombing to Irgun and records 91 deaths.

records.text: Owens cited Wikipedia as saying Canaanism was founded in 1939, peaked among Jews in Mandatory Palestine during the 1940s, and included former Irgun or Lehi members.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It reads, it tells you that Irgun was a Jewish Canaanite. Canaanism was a cultural and ideological movement founded in 1939, reaching its peak among the Jews of mandatory Palestine during the 1940s. It had a significant effect on the course of Israeli art, literature and spiritual and political thought. Its adherents were called Canaanites. OK, and then it tells you.

verification.notes: The current Canaanism article contains all three cited details: founding in 1939, peak influence among Jews in Mandatory Palestine in the 1940s, and that most members were former Irgun or Lehi members. This verifies the citation claim, not every broader characterization made around it.

sources.title: Canaanism
sources.relevance: The cited Wikipedia entry contains the dates and former Irgun/Lehi membership language summarized in the statement.
